8e4da78b-42b8-4775-8e0d-02bf8396f2bc.one_liner: A single-name leveraged finance case study on Chobani's dramatic spread tightening illustrates how far HY/CCC relative value has compressed, a useful read-through for anyone pricing credit risk in that cohort.
8e4da78b-42b8-4775-8e0d-02bf8396f2bc.recap: 9fin's Syndication Nation podcast covers Chobani's transformation from a niche, capacity-constrained Greek yogurt maker into the largest yogurt brand in the US, and how that has reshaped its standing in leveraged finance markets. Reporter David Wessenhaver explains that Chobani has issued debt for about a decade, but pricing has compressed sharply: an April issuance of triple-C-plus/B3 rated senior unsecured notes priced at 6.375%, roughly 225bps tighter than the average for that rating cohort and the tightest print of the year at those ratings. A term loan priced at SOFR+2025bps at par in October 2025, versus SOFR+375bps at 99.5 in 2023. Growth has been driven by the protein/low-sugar trend (aided by GLP-1 drugs boosting protein demand) and diversification via acquisitions of La Colombe coffee and Daily Harvest. Despite bullish fundamentals, several investors told Wessenhaver they are stepping back — not on credit quality concerns but because spreads no longer compensate for triple-C risk. Operating cash flow rose from $107mm (FY2022) to $584mm (FY2025), but free cash flow remains negative due to heavy capex (~$900mm projected this fiscal year) funding a $1.2bn New York plant, $500mm Idaho plant, and ~$570mm Michigan coffee facility. Risks flagged include competitive entry by larger packaged-food players (e.g., Pepsi/Yum) undercutting on price, and execution risk on the capex-heavy diversification strategy.
terms: SOFR -- Secured Overnight Financing Rate, the US risk-free reference rate used for floating-rate loan pricing
CCC/B3 -- speculative-grade credit ratings (S&P/Moody's) denoting higher default risk within high-yield
